scope: 12 complete GPT families: AA, pp, pm, mm member pairs; each has a/p/m targets

candidate3.change: Keep 9 immutable sanitized rho matrices; share identical physical inputs across families
candidate3.exactness: Same finite-or-positive-zero transform. No pair scan, block partition, or Acc merge edits. Kernel source is immutably borrowed. Invalid original-rho checks remain unchanged.
candidate3.lifetime: SharedRho owns its clean Vecs and borrows the original Kernel; returned slices borrow SharedRho. Compiler rejects dangling views and original source mutation. Owner drops after synchronous family scans complete.
candidate3.unknown: No full candidate3 build, full-market equivalence run, or elapsed-time measurement yet. Cache/bandwidth benefit and sequential 9-matrix preparation cost are unknown.
candidate3.note: Whole-market scan working-set savings are calculated bytes, not measured peak RSS; families can finish at different times.

other_exact_reuse.item: Pair normalizing weights are independent of target direction c

source.evidence: let d2 = ea[i] + eb[j] + 2. * r * sa[i] * sb[j]
let (wi, wj) = ((sa[i] / d) as f32, (sb[j] / d) as f32)

other_exact_reuse.feasibility: Exact if computed with the existing expression and reused without recomputing from reciprocals. Full 4-group dense f32 weight-pair cache would add 4*8*n*n bytes; block-local three-target grouping avoids a full cache but requires a larger scan refactor.
other_exact_reuse.priority: Lower than input sharing: O(n^2) weight work versus O(n^3) score processing; no measured seconds saved.

other_exact_reuse.item: Input finite checks and direction vectors repeat
other_exact_reuse.feasibility: Can validate each direction pair once with the same positive-energy masks, but would alter which family-specific error is reported first. Candidate3 deliberately keeps these checks unchanged.
other_exact_reuse.priority: Preparatory O(n^2) work; not an explanation for all of the roughly minute-long scan.

not_exact_shortcuts.idea: Reconstruct all-event rho/H from buy/sell rho/H
not_exact_shortcuts.why_not: Kernel normalizes component sums in f64 and then stores separate rho entries as f32. Recombining already-rounded direction rho values changes rounding; H/G maxima, top-K and positive masks are nonlinear.

source.evidence: let numerator = component_sum(&lead, i * n + j, a, b)

not_exact_shortcuts.idea: Reuse complete H/G arrays or top-K results across different target directions
not_exact_shortcuts.why_not: p, q, target validity and hence H/G values all depend on c. Only weights share exactly; no general identical score result was found beyond existing same-direction/mirror reuse.
